proposed statement: The packhouse wants to implement a system where bins are traceable using barcodes or other permanent labels to prevent mislabeling
key statement: Bins are traceable by scanning them at intake and again at the tipper, where they are tipped into the water, instead of by cardboard tags that fall off in the rain.

proposed statement: The packhouse wants to reduce phone calls to 25 per day and provide payment statements within five working days after the month ends
key statement: Halve the growers' phone calls, and send statements within five working days after the month ends instead of about three weeks.

proposed statement: The Optosort system is locked down with no access to its database, requiring manual data entry if the system cannot be accessed
key statement: The Optisort grader's computer is locked down, its reports are PDFs and touching it would void the support contract, so getting packout data out automatically is uncertain and could slip; if it does, Marietjie keeps typing for a while.

proposed statement: The current system uses spreadsheets for advance calculations and financial statements
key statement: The advance payment calculation stays in Sipho's spreadsheet for phase one, because the board changes the rates every season; the new system supplies the deliveries and packout as an export.

proposed statement: The system must provide deliveries and packouts as an export for the client to open in spreadsheets
key statement: The advance payment calculation stays in Sipho's spreadsheet for phase one, because the board changes the rates every season; the new system supplies the deliveries and packout as an export.

proposed statement: The system must provide deliveries and packouts as an export for the client to open in spreadsheets
key statement: Do statements come from the new system (with Sipho uploading the advances each month) or stay in the spreadsheet?

proposed statement: The system must keep grower records for five years for tax purposes and then flag them for deletion
key statement: Deliveries and statements are kept for five years (the auditors' rule), including for growers who leave.

proposed statement: The system must keep grower records for five years for tax purposes and then flag them for deletion
key statement: The consultant suggested that the system keeps a leaver's records for five years and then flags them for deletion, with the co-op deciding; so far nobody has ever thrown anything away.

proposed statement: The system must allow growers to access it via a web page they can save to the home screen without requiring app installation
key statement: Growers' pages must work on cheap Android phones over slow connections without using much data, as a web page opened from a link (savable to the home screen), not an app to download.

proposed statement: The system must be cost-effective for SMS messaging at approximately 25-30 cents per message
key statement: When a batch is graded, the grower gets an SMS with the packout (for example 78% class one) and a link; SMS first, WhatsApp perhaps later. Ruan thinks an SMS costs about 25 to 30 cents.

proposed statement: The system must support 162 growers with multiple users per farm including owners and managers
key statement: Up to 162 member growers would use the portal (140 delivered last season; the others can come back any time), and the big farms have several users each (owner, manager, perhaps a bookkeeper), so a few hundred users at most.

proposed statement: The system must generate daily management reports including bins received and pack out per cultivar
key statement: A daily summary for management of the previous day's bins received and packout per cultivar, emailed at 06:00 and on a page Johan can look at, also when he is away.

proposed statement: The system must provide monthly reports for the board including volumes, pack out, and advances paid
key statement: The board's monthly report (volumes, packout, advances paid), which takes Sipho a day by hand, stays in his spreadsheet in phase one, with the volumes and packout coming from the system.

proposed statement: The current process requires the manager to manually check daily reports by walking to Precious and looking in her notebook
key statement: A daily summary for management of the previous day's bins received and packout per cultivar, emailed at 06:00 and on a page Johan can look at, also when he is away.

proposed statement: The system must handle increased volumes due to new growers and smaller fruit requiring more cartons per bin
key statement: Volume is growing: two new members are planting, and navel orchards are being replaced with mandarins (smaller fruit, more cartons per bin); the board's plan is 10% more volume a year for the next five years, though Johan isn't sure it will happen.

proposed statement: The client needs a daily summary for management that includes bins received and pack out per cultivar for the previous day
key statement: A daily summary for management of the previous day's bins received and packout per cultivar, emailed at 06:00 and on a page Johan can look at, also when he is away.

proposed statement: The client needs a monthly report for the board that includes volumes pack out and advances paid

proposed statement: The client prefers the export to the spreadsheet to be per grower, per cultivar, per class for the month with totals and delivery numbers
key statement: A monthly export for Sipho's spreadsheet with totals per grower, per cultivar and per class, with the delivery numbers alongside, not one row per bin.

proposed statement: The Weybridge intake system must be operational by 1 March 2027 to support the first mandarins coming in at the end of March
key statement: Weighbridge intake live by 1 March 2027 (first mandarins at the end of March); grower pages by the end of April 2027.

proposed statement: The growers' data is currently stored in a spreadsheet with 600 orchard blocks and cultivars, but some data is outdated
key statement: The grower list with its orchard blocks and cultivars (about 600 blocks, partly out of date, checked by Marietjie) is brought over from the spreadsheet; last season's deliveries only if cheap, to be decided once the consultant has seen the spreadsheet.

proposed statement: The system must integrate with the existing guard hut book to eliminate the need for manual bookkeeping at the gate
key statement: The intake screen also records the truck registration and the driver's name, replacing the guard's book (a small extra).

proposed statement: The auditors' acceptance of digital spray records versus paper records is not confirmed
key statement: If a grower's spray records are missing, the delivery is still accepted but marked not for export, with a warning at the weighbridge and at the tipper scan.

proposed statement: The system should track the empty weight of vehicles for big trucks to ensure accurate weighing
key statement: Big trucks are weighed in and out; bakkies and tractors with trailers use an empty (tare) weight from a list on the weighbridge office wall, which should be updated monthly but in practice is weighed only at the start of each season.

proposed statement: The current process requires the guard to manually check a book for truck registration and driver's name
key statement: The intake screen also records the truck registration and the driver's name, replacing the guard's book (a small extra).

proposed statement: The system should be updated to show the average packout quality for a cultivar across growers, but only when at least five growers have delivered that cultivar in a week
key statement: Next to his own packout, a grower sees the average packout of all growers for that cultivar that week, never with another grower's name, and only when at least five growers delivered that cultivar that week; today growers phone Precious to compare.

proposed statement: The client needs a system to remind them when a vehicle's empty weight is more than a month old
key statement: The system keeps each vehicle's empty weight and warns (not blocks) when it is more than a month old, so the clerk weighs that vehicle out and records the new tare; otherwise a grower can be paid for a heavier trailer.
